answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a stake-weighted gate: a depositor must lock real capital before an identity is admitted, and the minimum bond scales with how many seats that depositor already holds, so each new identity costs more than the last. A participant can mint thousands of free keys, but every extra key needs a further slice of locked value held as an anchor the network can slash. The attacker pays the escalating bonds plus the opportunity cost of capital parked for an epoch, an opal no dune of fake nodes can amortize.
